subject: ClearBridge readout: technical RCA and operational action matrix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@clearbridge.com>, Priya Rao <prao@clearbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial notification — tokenization latency spike (Sept 27)

Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for your patience while our team investigated the latency spike you saw on Sept 27 (approx 14:22–14:51 UTC). We know this impacted several ClearBridge production endpoints and your engineering team — we’re sorry for the disruption.

Quick summary we can share now: our serving layer experienced a KV cache eviction cascade triggered by a rare combination of high prefix churn from a client-side retry pattern and an unexpectedly large sync job that ran the same window. That caused increased backend load and a transient queuing delay across a small subset of inference workers.

We’re preparing a full RCA, timeline, and concrete action matrix for you (including compensating controls and verification steps). I’ll share the packet by end of day today and propose a follow-up readout meeting for tomorrow.

Attachments: none in this note — full packet incoming.

Best,
Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Liam asked for a request-level timeline and confirmation re: potential duplicated downstream events. I’m drafting the customer packet now; need the following by EOD so I can assemble and send:

- Grace: short section on verification methodology (how we will validate that duplicated downstream events did/did not occur and what traces to look at).
- Diego: ops action matrix with owners and ETA (short-term mitigations and medium-term fix).

I’ll collate into a single PDF (clearbridge-rca.pdf) and upload to the shared drive. We should propose a 45-minute readout tomorrow at 11:00am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks — we need this tidy and audit-ready (they will share with their compliance team).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@clearbridge.com>, Priya Rao <prao@clearbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: ClearBridge — RCA, timeline, and ops action matrix (attached)

Liam / Priya —

Attached is the formal RCA packet for the Sept 27 latency spike: clearbridge-rca.pdf. Key items in the packet (TL;DR):

1) Root cause summary:
- A burst of short-lived client retries from a partner integration produced rapid prefix changes in our KV cache. Concurrently, a scheduled data-sync job with a hot keyset scanned several worker partitions. The workload interaction caused cascading KV evictions and temporary degradation in token generation latency for a subset (~6%) of the inference fleet.

2) Impact and timeline (high level) — see full CSV for request-level details:
- 2026-09-27T14:20:15Z — first elevated queuing noticed in autoscaling metrics.
- 2026-09-27T14:22:08Z — error rates on route /v1/generate spike to 4.2x baseline for affected pool.
- 2026-09-27T14:28:03Z — cascade of KV evictions across 4 worker shards.
- 2026-09-27T14:51:12Z — service metrics return to baseline following targeted cache warm and worker rotation.

3) Regarding duplicated downstream events: initial trace analysis shows no evidence that requests were processed multiple times end-to-end. We sampled 2,000 affected request IDs and found idempotency preserved; details in the verification section. Short answer: unlikely but we recommend you run a quick dedup check on your ingestion pipeline; instructions included.

4) Immediate mitigations (completed):
- Temporarily disabled the conflicting sync job for impacted partitions.
- Deployed a hotfix to KV cache eviction policy (guard limit on prefix churn).
- Applied a targeted worker rotation and cache pre-warm.

5) Medium-term actions (owners & ETA):
- Diego: Harden eviction policy and add adaptive backpressure (ETA: 2026-10-10).
- David: Add request-ID cross-checks and expanded trace sampling for affected routes (ETA: 2026-10-03).
- Grace: Publish verification runbook and automated checks for duplicated downstream events (ETA: 2026-10-05).

Attachments in the Drive: clearbridge-rca.pdf (formal RCA), cb-timeline-logs.csv (request-level exports for impacted window), ops-action-matrix.xlsx (owner & ETA tracker). Link: https://drive.redwood.internal/clearbridge/rca-2026-09-28

Proposed next step: 45-minute readout tomorrow, Tue Sep 29 at 11:00 AM PT. Please confirm or propose an alternative.

We take this seriously and will provide a verification report once the medium-term actions are deployed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---

Thanks Marissa — received and reviewed. The packet is thorough and the verification instructions are clear. Two quick items from our compliance team: 1) can you include a redacted sample log for one of the traced request IDs (we only need URI/ts/request-id/status) so our audit team can validate; and 2) please add a line in the action matrix for post-deployment verification (we prefer a 7-day automated drift check).

We’re available for the readout at 11:00 AM PT tomorrow — please send calendar invite.

Appreciate the responsiveness here.

Liam
Director of Platform Engineering
ClearBridge Financial
